answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, verifiable resource at its kernel — for example, a small bonded deposit that is slashed on provable misbehavior. One cheap identity is easy; thousands become expensive. Like a pearl forming only around a real grain of sand, reputation accrues only to identities with sustained, attested work history, and an onyx-hard audit trail lets peers verify that history instead of trusting self-claims. Attackers face real cost per fake, so fakes stop paying.
